clinician.trajectory_summary: A 34-year-old unmarried woman presented with a 2-month history of left lower abdominal lump and pain associated with intermittent fever and chills. Physical examination revealed pallor and a left lower abdominal mass measuring 10x8.5 cm on vaginal examination. Initial laboratory investigations including hemogram, liver and renal function tests, and tumor markers were normal; serology for HBsAg, HCV, and HIV were negative. CECT abdomen revealed a heterogeneous enhancing solid-cystic lesion with septations measuring 10x9.5x9.0 cm in the left ovary. Surgical resection of the left ovary was performed. Gross pathology showed a mass measuring 11 x 9.0 x 8.5 cm with an encapsulated outer surface, light yellow serous fluid, and cystic/solid areas with black pigmentation. Histopathological examination using HE and PAS staining demonstrated dense inflammation, necrosis, and florid fungal septate hyphae with dichotomous branching, confirming the diagnosis of ovarian aspergillosis. Post-diagnosis imaging (CECT thorax) ruled out pulmonary involvement. The patient was treated with intravenous voriconazole (6 mg/kg/day) and liposomal amphotericin B (0.5 mg/kg/day) for 10 days.
